newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt off all-time highs, but uptrend intact.
newsitem.headline: German debt off all-time highs, but uptrend intact.

text.p: German debt was trading off its record intraday highs in late dealings but with gloomy signals for the German economy abounding, traders expected the market to remain in a broad uptrend.
March Bund futures were up 20 basis points at 103.83 at 1532 GMT, dragged off an intraday high of 104.4 by declines on the U.S. market, but seen with plenty of chances to resume their advance.
"We can't seem to take our eyes off Treasuries but if they hold mainly steady, we will see that 104 and even 105 (on the future) again with no trouble," said a Frankfurt dealer.
On the cash market, benchmark 10-year Bunds were at 103.89, up from 103.77 for a yield of 5.48 percent.

Looking ahead to further German domestic data, dealers said they did not expect a major influence on the market from January German M3 data, which is likely to be released some time this week. They noted that January M3 data is volatile.
"There are absolutely no negative decisions on the way that could harm the German market at the moment. The Bundesbank, especially, is not going to take any action," the trader added.

The market's bullish tone is underpinned by broad conviction that the dollar is too strong against the mark to allow the Bundesbank to take any action on interest rates when its policymaking council meets on Thursday.
There had been speculation in recent months that there was room for a slight easing of monetary policy to boost the German economy, but the rise of the dollar is seen as tying the Bundesbank's hands.
